verdict.rationale: Supermemory's own docs clearly support ingesting non-chat content: raw documents, files and URLs, type-aware extraction for PDFs, images, video and code, and connectors that sync Google Drive, Notion, Gmail, OneDrive and GitHub. JSON is never named as a supported input, structured business data is only implied through the connectors, and one hands-on report says a large link failed to ingest because the content was too large. missing for 10: explicit documented JSON/structured-data ingestion, explicit business-data (e.g. database/CRM record) ingestion, documented content size limits, independent hands-on corroboration of document ingestion at scale.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ingest documents, JSON, and business data into memory — not just chat transcripts

citations.quote: Send any raw content to Supermemory — conversations, documents, files, URLs. We extract the memories automatically.
Multi-modal Extractors | PDFs, images (OCR), videos (transcription), code (AST-aware chunking). Upload and it works.
Connect external platforms to automatically sync documents into supermemory. Supported connectors include Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, GitHub, Granola and Web Crawler
Ingest a conversation and a document, then use document search, memory graph traversal, and profiles
